name: Cor triatriatum dexter
aliases: Cor triatriatum of the right atrium

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic and imaging diagnostic criteria for cor triatriatum dexter

criteria.description: Presence of a fibromuscular membrane dividing the right atrium into two distinct chambers
Visualization of the membrane and associated flow obstruction on echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Evidence of right atrial inflow obstruction or elevated right atrial pressures on catheterization or Doppler studies
Exclusion of other congenital cardiac anomalies causing similar symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of the right atrial membrane causing chamber division with echocardiographic or imaging confirmation and evidence of hemodynamic obstruction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities; cardiac catheterization may be used for hemodynamic assessment.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Right atrial membrane causing chamber division
searchTerms: right atrial partition causing chamber split
blockage of blood flow into right atrium
restricted blood entry to right atrium

common.notes: May occur if associated with atrial septal defect
searchTerms: blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

common.notes: Secondary to elevated right atrial pressure

searchTerms: liver swelling from poor blood flow

rare.notes: Due to paradoxical embolism if shunting present
searchTerms: brain stroke or blood clot traveling in body
stroke or systemic blood clot event
right atrium heart muscle disease causing arrhythmia
heart rhythm disorder from right atrial disease

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to hepatic congestion
Possible hypoxemia on arterial blood gas if shunting present
imaging: Echocardiographic visualization of right atrial membrane
Cardiac MRI confirming membrane and chamber division
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Cardiac catheterization demonstrating elevated right atrial pressures

distinguishingFeatures: Membrane divides left atrium instead of right atrium
Symptoms related to pulmonary venous obstruction
Apical displacement of tricuspid valve leaflets
Right atrial enlargement without membranous partition

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of right heart failure in neonate or infant
Sudden onset syncope or neurological deficits
